newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha strengthens as fresh demand emerges.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha strengthens as fresh demand emerges.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices strengthened by around $10 a tonne on Tuesday boosted by trader short covering, signs of fresh end-user demand and transatlantic arbitrage possibilities, traders said.

The market was initially boosted by trader short covering after some players had sold short into end-user top-up demand. But physical demand was also seen with some German buyers seen looking for alternative product to cover against ice-blocked ARA barge supplies.

Traders said there had been some pressure on prices towards the end of December caused by traders pricing strategies, but rising prices and the scent of fresh end-user buying saw cargo holders withdrawing offers.
"Now the cheaper prices have been fixed and the buying is coming back into the market there are very few sellers around," one trader said.

Traders also eyed attractive U.S. prices for the possibility of transatlantic arbitrage, but although at least one Wall Street refiner was seen looking for product, very tight freight space was seen limiting this option.
"You can move anything if you can find a ship," one trader said.
Brazilian state refiner Petrobras was reported to be loading a large cargo at Skikda and is also expected to be seeking more product later in the month.
This product is expected to go transatlantic but some trader felt that it could be sold back into Europe if prices continued to strengthen.
Buying interest was seen for pipeline spec by Jan 20 at around high cif +$2 a tonne. Cargo offers were sharply higher at around $235 although nearest bids were pegged around $4-5 under this.
A second Egyptian Alex cargo was traded into Lavera at high cif +$2.75 a tonne and a Tunis fob stem were heard offered around high cif $5-6 a tonne.
